title: Glitchless category for Crown of Brine

posts.cooked:
Hey everyone, I wanted to start a thread focused on the Glitchless category for Crown of Brine speedruns. With all the crazy stuff people have been pulling off using glitches and duplicate tricks, I feel like it’s time to have a solid space dedicated just to runs that avoid any unintended game exploits. Plus, I think it really showcases skill and planning when you have to rely solely on the intended mechanics of the classic Mac build and the known modded versions.

I’ve been diving into the “solved” puzzles and sequences here, and it’s surprisingly satisfying to see how much you can optimize even without the usual shortcuts. Does anyone have any tips or optimized routes they’re testing out for this category? I feel like some of the duplicate item work might be off-limits here, so it’s a fresh challenge to rethink inventory management and time saves. Would love to hear your thoughts or see some personal bests!

Looking forward to building a good leaderboard and maybe even a starter guide for new runners interested in glitchless runs. Let’s keep it clean and competitive!

posts.cooked:
I totally get where you’re coming from about establishing a clear glitchless category for Crown of Brine, especially since the community keeps growing and players are finding so many wild exploits. Having a dedicated category that’s strictly glitch-free would definitely help standardize runs and give newcomers a fair baseline to compare against. It’s cool that the modded versions have introduced some shortcuts that blur the lines, but keeping a classic-mac duplicate run untouched preserves that original challenge feel.

Also, I think since the game is already considered solved from a completion standpoint, pushing the glitchless route could actually encourage more creative routing. You’d have runners scrambling to find the fastest sequence of legit moves and item uses without relying on game-breaking tricks. Honestly, it might even revitalize interest because the category is basically a fresh puzzle in its own right.

I’m curious if anyone has tried documenting a full glitchless route yet? I’ve seen some partial attempts floating around, but nothing fully fleshed out from start to finish that’s been verified. Once that happens, maybe the community can vote to have glitchless runs officially recognized on the leaderboard. It’s exciting times for Crown of Brine speedrunning!

posts.cooked:
Hey, I totally get where you’re coming from about wanting a true glitchless category for Crown of Brine. The modded runs are cool and all, and they can be really fast, but it’s refreshing to see someone try to beat the game without bending the rules or exploiting any unintended mechanics. It honestly feels like a pure test of skill and understanding the game’s core design rather than making the game do things it wasn’t meant to.

I’ve been running classic-mac versions myself, and the biggest challenge is managing the duplicate enemies without triggering any glitches. It’s kinda wild how subtle some of the game’s quirks can be when you go for glitchless—stuff like pathing AI and how the physics respond to scripted events. But that also makes every perfect strafe and well-timed jump feel way more satisfying.

Also, I think keeping this category separate from the modded runs preserves the community’s respect for both playstyles. Solved runs are awesome achievements, but glitchless feels like keeping the game’s original spirit alive. Would love to see more people posting their times here soon!

posts.cooked:
I’m really excited to see the interest growing around a glitchless category for Crown of Brine! It feels like the perfect way to honor the original design and challenge ourselves to master the game within its intended boundaries. Since the modded runs and duplicate exploits have dominated for a while, going glitchless brings a fresh kind of tension and strategy—especially on classic-mac where control precision matters so much.

One thing I’ve noticed lately while practicing is just how much the solved maps test your patience and route planning without shortcuts. The timing has to be spot on, but the game still allows enough room for creative movement if you’re careful. I think speedrunners who can consistently nail these routes will really highlight the depth of Crown’s mechanics, maybe even better than some glitch-heavy runs.

Has anyone tried setting up official leaderboards or verifying runs strictly on classic-mac hardware? I’d love to see more community involvement on that front to standardize the glitchless category. It’s kind of a different vibe, and it would be cool to have a separate leaderboard where all runs follow the same rules. Looking forward to any new strats or discoveries people come up with!

posts.cooked:
I totally get where you’re coming from about wanting a clean slate for the glitchless runs. Crown of Brine has so many little quirks that make glitches tempting to exploit, but sticking to a pure category really highlights the game’s design and the runner’s skill. Especially in that tricky section with the tidal caves, where you have to rely solely on timing instead of any frame-perfect skips — it feels way more rewarding to nail it without leaning on any known exploits.

Also, I’m curious if anyone else has tried the classic-mac mod for glitchless runs? I know it’s mostly for the visual tweaks, but some say it actually smooths out input lag enough to help with precise movement in the duplicate shrine sequence. If that’s true, it might be worth considering for runners who want the pure category but also the best performance possible without going full modded glitch runs.

Finally, shoutout to the community members who’ve been putting together those “solved” guides for puzzle rooms in glitchless mode. They’re incredibly helpful for planning routes that don’t rely on duplicating map fragments or other sneaky tricks. It feels like we’re really forging a solid foundation for Crown of Brine speedrunning that respects the game’s original spirit!

posts.cooked:
Hey, I totally get where you’re coming from wanting a dedicated glitchless category for Crown of Brine. Since the original game has so many sequences that are easily exploited, running it pure without any unintended skips or UI bugs really changes the flow and skill it takes. Plus, for folks who are more interested in the story or the carefully crafted mechanics, glitchless definitely feels more authentic.

I think it’s also worth mentioning that the modded versions with the “solved” patch make it easier to enforce glitchless runs since they block out a lot of those funky duplicate item issues and weird sequence breaks. The original classic-Mac build is legendary, but it’s kind of a double-edged sword—it’s charming, but it’s a nightmare to verify glitchless runs on sometimes. Having a glitchless leaderboard alongside the current categories, maybe even distinguishing between the classic and modded versions, would give everyone more room to compete fairly and enjoy the game from different angles.

Honestly, even if the glitchless runs end up taking longer, I’m all for it because it feels like a fresh puzzle each time you can’t just skip the tricky bits. Would love to see more runners pushing that category and maybe some community-organized races down the line!

posts.cooked:
Hey, I totally get where you’re coming from about wanting a solid glitchless category for Crown of Brine. The modded runs have been wild lately, but sometimes it feels like the classic mechanics get lost when people start abusing duplicates or weird item tricks. Having a glitchless category would help keep things grounded and pay homage to the original pacing and challenge of the game.

From what I’ve seen, the community is already making strides toward defining what “glitchless” really means here — no clipping through walls, no item duplication, and no sequence breaks that warp the intended progression. It’s encouraging because it means the runs become a true test of skill and route optimization rather than exploiting game faults. Plus, it’s always more satisfying to watch someone nail those tricky sections the way the devs probably intended.

I’m curious if anyone else has started recording segment times in this category? I’d be happy to help compile some verified benchmarks once the rules get locked down. It feels like this could be the next big thing if we get the community behind it and keep the leaderboard clean. Either way, I’m excited to see how this evolves!
